note: ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE names the provider file, and the adapter always sets it -- here too, where the fixture's empty home leaves nothing to carry into it. Replay calls the same prepare with the operator's current environment, so an adapter that redirected nothing there would let a replay run live on their real providers and still report success because nothing reached the proxy. Given a config it can read, the adapter writes a redirected copy instead; that path is checked in test/zcode.test.ts. ZCode's file is JSON, so the rewrite parses a tree and walks every node rather than matching text. An earlier version of this note said that settled the completeness question MiniMax Code's YAML rewrite kept answering wrongly; it does not, and review found the gap. Parsing locates values and says nothing about which are secret: isSecret knew apiKey and api_key and not APIKEY, Authorization or jwt, and isOrigin knew baseUrl and not endpoint, host or url -- so a credential under an unanticipated name was copied into the run directory, and from there into trace/. Fixed the way MiniMax Code arrived at: the rewrite stays an allowlist because it must produce correct output, origins are now recognised by value rather than key name, and a value-shaped net over the result refuses anything it cannot account for. The net's opaque-token alphabet keeps - and _ as MiniMax Code's does, and excludes only /. An earlier version took the separators out, because ZCode's shipped provider.example.json has "type": "zhipu-coding-plan-api-key" -- 25 characters of exactly those, an enum value -- and removing them was how that file stopped being refused. Review measured the compensating claim and it was false: abc123-abc123-abc123-abc123 has entropy about 2.8 bits per character against a 4.0 threshold and deadbeef-deadbeef-deadbeef has no digit, so the redactor declines both, and with the separators out the shape net never saw them either. Measured in a real recording: three such values under api.headers -- which PROVIDER_CONFIG.md documents as an arbitrary string map, and where a gateway's signed header lives -- landed verbatim in the run directory. The separators are back and the false positive is answered by naming the four fields whose values are identifiers (type, modelId, personalModelIds, modelOrder), exempt from the shape check only and still read by the redactor. The launch overlay also blanks ZCode's whole environment namespace before naming the file. Measured: the bundle names 200 ZCODE_* variables and reads them through minified constants (Hee="ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE", read as process.env[Hee]), so which are live cannot be established by grep -- among them ZCODE_BASE_URL, ZCODE_ENDPOINT_ORIGIN and three more origins, ZCODE_CREDENTIAL_SECRET and two more credentials, plus ZAI_*, BIGMODEL_*, GLM_* and OPENAI_/ANTHROPIC_ base-url and key pairs the bundle also names. With all of them blanked ZCode still boots and captures in full, measured. Verified against zcode-runtime 0.16.9 (zcode-app-cli 3.14.1-27, a wrapper whose zcode-runtime.lock.json records the official ZCode-3.14.1-linux-x64.deb and its sha512) by running it: `orca record zcode -- --prompt '...' --mode yolo` recorded a request carrying a 9,084-character system prompt beginning 'You are ZCode, an interactive coding agent' and 27 tools, and `orca replay` reproduced it offline with reused=1/1, exact=1, divergences=0, unmatched=0, egress=blocked -- the replayed error carrying the recording's own requestId. Four things measured rather than assumed. ZCODE_HOME does NOT relocate ~/.zcode, so the adapter cannot isolate the way MiniMax Code's does. An empty ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE makes ZCode refuse to start, so the eight account-backed built-in providers are not redirected and a run on one of them is not captured; the sweep blanks that variable instead, which leaves ZCode reading its own bundled file. A model id orca invented ends the run at `Model creation failed` before a request exists, which is why the fallback config names glm-4.6 -- and --model is not a flag this harness has at all (`Unknown option '--model'`), so the model is chosen in the config and `capture.mjs zcode` takes none. Finally, the prompt embeds three facts about the directory it runs in rather than the harness -- the git branch, the git status output, and its per-project memory directory name, which is <basename>-<16 hex of the absolute path>. capture.mjs scrubs all three to placeholders, so the artifact no longer depends on where it was captured: measured, the same capture taken inside this repository on a dirty feature branch and in an empty repository on master produce byte-identical files. The as-sent length still differs (9,084 against 9,525), which is what the capture README's column records.
